run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T22:53:45Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend matches a burst of frontend ERROR spans that began in the minute ending 2026-11-16T22:53:45Z and grew to about 0.9/s per failing span by 23:00:45. The only failing frontend path is its ad dependency: the 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' client spans error (116.3 per 5m, 112.8 of them finishing in under 10 ms) together with the 'GET /api/data' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' spans, while GET /, GET /api/cart, GET /api/products/{productId}, GET /api/recommendations, POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout show no ERROR spans. The ad side is the failing dependency: pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5 (Deployment ad, replicas=1) has its only container 'ad' repeatedly terminated with reason OOMKilled and exit code 137 (lastState finished 22:54:59, current state finished 22:56:01), Ready=False since 22:56:02 with 'containers with unready status: [ad]', a Warning BackOff event with count 23 at 23:00:38, and the ad Endpoints object holds only notReadyAddresses for that pod. ad's own span rate fell from ~1.74/s to 0 between 22:52:45 and 22:58:45 and stayed 0, and the ad container's cAdvisor working set was already growing (331 MB at 22:27:45 to 372 MB at 22:53:45) before a rapid series of container restarts. frontend-proxy recorded its own 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' ERROR spans rising in the same minutes. Whether the ad process leaks or the 450Mi limit is simply too small cannot be determined from the available data: ad's JVM metrics are not scraped, its logs end at 22:51:50, Jaeger returned no traces, and the frontend pod produced no readable logs.

claims.text: Frontend ERROR spans first appear in the scrape at 2026-11-16T22:53:45Z (5m error rate 0 at 22:52:45): span_name='GET', 'GET /api/data', 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' each 0.1222/s and span_name='tcp.connect' 0.0333/s, rising to ~0.9/s for the four main spans by 23:00:45 and decaying after 23:04:45.

Summed by service, frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate was 0 at 22:52:45, 1.359/s at 22:54:45, 3.011/s at 22:56:45 and 3.615/s at 23:00:45; in the same series only ad, fraud-detection and recommendation show ~0.0037/s blips (present before 22:53 and later, i.e. background) and accounting and payment stay at 0.

frontend-proxy recorded its own STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans for span_name='ingress' and span_name='router frontend egress': 0.0148/s and 0/s around 22:50, 0.1333/s and 0.1259/s at 22:53:00, and about 1.09/s and 1.07/s at 23:02:00.

In the 5 minutes ending 23:04:45 the frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' client span had 116.3 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, 112.8 of them in the le=10.0 ms bucket and 108.2 in the le=2.0 bucket, while the same span with STATUS_CODE_UNSET increased by 0 — the failures were immediate, not timeouts.

At 23:00:45 the frontend server span 'GET /api/data' increased by 270 per 5m, the same magnitude as its ~0.9/s error rate over that window, so the ERROR spans account for essentially all /api/data spans; in the same window 'GET /' 87.8, 'GET /api/cart' 233.3, 'GET /api/recommendations' 234.4 and 'POST /api/checkout' 150 spans had no ERROR spans in the error-span breakdown.

The ad service's own span rate by status_code fell from 1.7407/s (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) at 22:52:45 to 1.0259/s at 22:54:45, 0.1407/s at 22:56:45 and 0 from 22:58:45 onward; ad's STATUS_CODE_ERROR series stayed at 0 apart from ~0.0037/s blips before 22:53.
At 23:04:45 the 5m span increase was 0 for ad while other services were active: frontend 7365.8, frontend-proxy 3332.3, cart 2672.5, product-catalog 1792.8, checkout 1347.2.

Pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5 (namespace otel-demo) has container 'ad' with ready=false and restartCount 4; lastState.terminated.reason=OOMKilled exitCode=137 finished 22:54:59 (started 22:54:29) and state.terminated.reason=OOMKilled exitCode=137 finished 22:56:01 (started 22:55:50); pod condition Ready=False, reason ContainersNotReady, message 'containers with unready status: [ad]', lastTransitionTime 22:56:02.

Events in otel-demo for pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5: Normal Pulled/Created/Started (container ad) at 22:57:30 with count 6, and Warning BackOff at 23:00:38 with message 'Back-off restarting failed container ad in pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5_otel-demo(...)' count 23.
Of the 21 pods in otel-demo, only ad-554b849958-l9ft5 is not ready (phase Running, READY false, restarts 4); frontend-675fd7b5c5-jfvbx and the other 19 pods are ready=true with restartCount 0.
Deployment 'ad' in otel-demo reports unavailableReplicas=1 with readyReplicas and availableReplicas absent, while every other deployment in the namespace reports ready=1 and available=1.

The Endpoints object 'ad' in otel-demo has no ready addresses at all: its only subset contains notReadyAddresses [{ip 100.96.2.230, nodeName i-0d81a0f472ebdc704, targetRef Pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5}] for port tcp-service/8080.

The ad container's resources are limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi and requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi; Deployment ad was created 2026-11-16T22:15:21Z with replicas 1 and the container template that uses image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, and ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 (created 22:15:21Z) is owned by Deployment ad.

container_memory_working_set_bytes for pod ad-554b849958-l9ft5 / container ad shows container instance 0660c518… rising from 331,190,272 B at 22:27:45 to 371,867,648 B at 22:53:45 with no further samples, and then six further container IDs appearing in quick succession (c20195012a… 66.8 MB from 22:52:45, d11f8bdc… 59.4 MB at 22:53:45 then 183.8 MB, a72e9cb8… 2.6 MB at 22:54:45 then 49.0 MB, baa263fb… 2.3 MB from 22:56:45, 4d341002… 41.2 MB then 123.6 MB, 3b56c468… 2.6 MB then 189.2 MB from 23:02:45) — i.e. repeated container restarts with fast memory growth.

The flagd-config ConfigMap in otel-demo defines the ad fault-injection flags adFailure, adHighCpu and adManualGc with defaultVariant 'off' (variants off=false/on=true); no ad-related flag is enabled in the stored configuration.

Span-derived counters stop incrementing after about 23:01:45: in the window 23:01:45–23:06:45 the increase was 0 for every frontend server span (GET, GET /, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, GET /api/products/{productId}, GET /api/recommendations, POST, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout), for the frontend GetAds span and for all ad spans.

The ad container's readable log stream (2,678 lines, current instance only) contains ordinary request handling such as 'Targeted ad request received for [assembly]' and 'no baggage found in context' and ends at 2026-11-16T22:51:50Z; the container has no previous instance available in the node's log.

The underlying trigger of the ad container's memory growth is either a leak in the ad process or a 450Mi limit that is too small for its workload; the working set was already 331 MB at 22:27:45 and climbed about 1.5 MB/min to 372 MB by 22:53:45 before the restarts, but ad's JVM heap/GC metrics are not scraped (jvm_memory_* exists only for otel-collector) and its logs end at 22:51:50, so leak versus undersized limit cannot be decided.

Node-level memory pressure is not the cause: all five nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure=False (reason KubeletHasSufficientMemory), so the OOM kill of the ad container is not explained by node memory pressure.

The frontend itself as origin of the errors was considered and rejected: the frontend pod is ready with restartCount 0, its non-ad routes (GET /, GET /api/cart, GET /api/products/{productId}, GET /api/recommendations, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout) carry no ERROR spans in the same window, and its failing GetAds client spans return in under 10 ms, which is an immediate upstream failure rather than frontend-side latency or failure.

An enabled ad fault-injection flag was considered and rejected as the cause of this error burst: adFailure, adHighCpu and adManualGc are all defaultVariant 'off' in the flagd-config ConfigMap, and ad itself produced no ERROR spans before it stopped serving (its spans were STATUS_CODE_UNSET and then zero), which does not match a flag that makes the service return failures.

A rollout or pod replacement was considered and rejected: Deployment ad has existed since 22:15:21Z with an unchanged container template and image, its single ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 also dates from 22:15:21Z, the ad pod kept its name with restartCount 4 (in-place container restarts), and the only ad events are container Pulled/Created/Started plus BackOff — no SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete of a new pod.

Investigate and fix the ad container's memory behavior: profile the ad service heap, decide whether the 450Mi limit (225Mi request) is adequate, and either remove the growth or raise the limit so the single ad replica stops being OOMKilled.

Consider running more than one ad replica (Deployment ad has replicas=1) so that a single OOM-killed pod does not leave the ad Service with zero ready endpoints and take down the frontend /api/data route.

Have the team restore trace retention/collection and add ad-service JVM metric scraping so the gRPC status returned to the frontend and the piling heap can be verified directly rather than inferred from span counters alone; this dataset scrapes jvm_memory_* only for otel-collector-564d9c7987-psc5t.

gaps: Jaeger trace searches for frontend and ad (22:53:30–22:56:00 and 23:05:00–23:11:01) and tag searches error=true / otel.status_code=ERROR returned no traces (status no_data), so HTTP/gRPC status codes and parent-child call edges could not be read from traces; the Jaeger service list does contain frontend and ad.
The frontend pod's logs returned no lines for 22:50–23:05 and no previous container instance exists, so the frontend's own error text could not be read.
The ad container's log stream ends at 22:51:50Z and the previous container instance was unavailable (HTTP 400), so nothing was observed at the moment of the OOM kills.

ad's JVM metrics (jvm_memory_used_bytes, jvm_memory_used_after_last_gc_bytes, etc.) are scraped only for otel-collector-564d9c7987-psc5t; the ad service's heap and GC state are unknown, so leak versus undersized limit remains undecided.

kube-state-metrics workload/pod series (kube_deployment_status_replicas_available, kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready, kube_pod_*) returned no data, so workload availability and restart history before 22:53 could not be read; only cluster state at query time (~23:11–23:13) was observed.

The alerting rule 'RequestErrorRate' was not found in the loaded rule groups (list_prometheus_rules returned no data), so the exact alert expression and the source of the reported value 2.6222 are unverified.
http_server_request_duration_seconds_count has no series in this window, so frontend HTTP status codes are unknown.

Span-derived counters stop incrementing after about 23:01:45; whether the frontend error condition persisted to the end of the authorized window at 23:11:01 is unknown, although the ad Deployment still reported unavailableReplicas=1 at 23:12:07.
Only four events exist in otel-demo for the window (all for the ad pod, from 22:57:30), so restart/OOM history before that is unknown and events in other namespaces were not listed.
flagd's runtime flag state could not be read (configmap defaults only; flagd pod logs returned zero lines), so a runtime flag change cannot be fully excluded.
The 'change_history' integration is not available, so no deployment or configuration change record could be checked.
next_steps: Have the team confirm the ad service's memory profile and decide whether the 450Mi container limit or the ad process itself needs fixing.

Have the team verify whether the ad container was OOM-killed before 22:53 (kubelet events/restart metrics are unavailable in this dataset) and whether the alert condition is still active after 23:01:45.
Have the team confirm the RequestErrorRate rule definition and the source of the reported value 2.6222.
Advise restoring Jaeger retention/trace collection and adding ad-service JVM metric scraping so this failure path can be validated directly.
